title: Cocycle and identity laws for normalized ringed-topos derived composition
statement:
Let $X_0\xrightarrow f X_1\xrightarrow g X_2\xrightarrow h X_3$ be morphisms of ringed topoi presented by small sites, with structural maps between sheaves of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Write $R_f=Rf_*$, and similarly for the other morphisms. Let $\kappa_{g,f}:R_{gf}\xrightarrow{\sim}R_gR_f$ be the K-injective normalized comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. Then, suppressing functor associators,
$$(R_h\kappa_{g,f})\circ\kappa_{h,gf}=(\kappa_{h,g}R_f)\circ\kappa_{hg,f}.$$
The identity comparisons $\epsilon_X:R_{\mathrm{id}_X}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}$ are induced by termwise identity direct image, and satisfy
$$(\epsilon_{X_1}R_f)\circ\kappa_{\mathrm{id}_{X_1},f}=1_{R_f},\qquad(R_f\epsilon_{X_0})\circ\kappa_{f,\mathrm{id}_{X_0}}=1_{R_f}.$$
These laws also apply when one or more morphisms are coefficient changes on the identity underlying topos.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition; associativity and identity normalization extracted by the total-derived universal property

proof.text: Work first at $Q_0I$ with $I$ K-injective on $X_0$, writing $Q_i$ for localization on $X_i$. The ringed-topos definition supplies additive termwise direct images; use their canonical underived composition identifications throughout. Choose K-injective resolutions $j:f_*I\to J$, $k:g_*J\to K$, and $t:g_*f_*I\to T$, available on the small ringed sites by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. The normalization of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] says $g_*j$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Thus $k\circ g_*j$ is also a quasi-isomorphism. Neither $f_*I$ nor $g_*J$ is assumed K-injective.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition; explicit coherence calculation using derived.tex Tags 070I (lemma-K-injective) and 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined)

proof.text: Since $T$ and $K$ are K-injective, [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] represents the derived morphism $Q_2(k\circ g_*j)\circ(Q_2t)^{-1}:Q_2T\to Q_2K$ by a unique homotopy class $u:T\to K$. Moreover $u\circ t$ and $k\circ g_*j$ are homotopic: their images under $Q_2$ agree, and the same cited Hom bijection applies with source $g_*f_*I$ and K-injective target $K$. This is a comparison between actual resolutions, with no claim that termwise direct image preserves K-injectives.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition; explicit coherence calculation using derived.tex Tags 070I (lemma-K-injective) and 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined)

proof.text: Compute $(\kappa_{h,g}R_f)\circ\kappa_{hg,f}$ at $Q_0I$. The comparison for $(hg,f)$, using $j$, is represented by $(hg)_*j=h_*g_*j$. The comparison for $(h,g)$ at $R_f(Q_0I)=Q_1J$, using $k$, is represented by $h_*k$. Both assertions are precisely the K-injective normalization of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. Hence this side, in the common source $Q_3(h_*g_*f_*I)$ and target $Q_3(h_*K)$, is $Q_3(h_*(k\circ g_*j))$. The identifications here are the canonical resolution identifications, not additional choices of the composition isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition; explicit coherence calculation using derived.tex Tags 070I (lemma-K-injective) and 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined)

proof.text: For the other side, $\kappa_{h,gf}$ is represented by $h_*t$, by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. The map $\kappa_{g,f}$ is $Q_2(g_*j)$. Apply [lem-sf-kinjective-derived-map-computation] to $h_*$, to this morphism, and to the resolutions $t:g_*f_*I\to T$ and $k:g_*J\to K$. Its representing map between K-injective targets is exactly $u$ from Step 2. Therefore $(R_h\kappa_{g,f})\circ\kappa_{h,gf}$ is $Q_3(h_*u)\circ Q_3(h_*t)=Q_3(h_*(u\circ t))$. Termwise application of the additive functor $h_*$ preserves the homotopy of Step 2: apply $h_*$ to the equation $ut-kg_*j=ds+sd$. Thus this equals $Q_3(h_*(k\circ g_*j))$, the expression in Step 3.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition; explicit coherence calculation using derived.tex Tags 070I (lemma-K-injective) and 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined)

proof.text: For any complex $M$ on $X_0$, choose a K-injective resolution $a:M\to I$. Naturality of the two composites in the cocycle square identifies their components at $Q_0M$ with their components at $Q_0I$ conjugated by the images of the isomorphism $Q_0a$. The equality just proved at $Q_0I$ therefore gives equality at $Q_0M$. Every derived object is represented by a complex (up to the canonical localization equivalence), so the natural transformations agree. Canonical changes of resolution are compatible by the identity and composition formulas of [lem-sf-kinjective-derived-map-computation].

source.place: Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition; explicit coherence calculation using derived.tex Tags 070I (lemma-K-injective) and 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined)

proof.text: Construct the identity comparison explicitly. For $a:N\to I$ a K-injective resolution on $X$, let $c_a:R_{\mathrm{id}_X}(QN)\xrightarrow{\sim}QI$ be the canonical resolution identification. Set $\epsilon_{X,QN}=(Qa)^{-1}\circ c_a$. For a derived morphism $v:QN\to QN'$ and resolutions $a:N\to I$, $b:N'\to J$, [lem-sf-kinjective-derived-map-computation] gives a representing class $w:I\to J$ with $Qw=Qb\circ v\circ(Qa)^{-1}$. Applying its formula for the identity functor gives $\epsilon_{X,QN'}R_{\mathrm{id}_X}(v)=v\epsilon_{X,QN}$. Its change-of-resolution formula proves independence of $a$. Thus these are a natural isomorphism to the identity; they are exactly those induced by termwise identity direct image. In particular at K-injective $I$, choosing $a=1_I$ makes $\epsilon_{X,QI}$ the identity under the canonical computation.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition; explicit coherence calculation using derived.tex Tags 070I (lemma-K-injective) and 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined)

proof.text: For the left unit law evaluate at K-injective $I$ on $X_0$, choose $j:f_*I\to J$ K-injective, and apply the normalization of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] with $g=\mathrm{id}_{X_1}$. It gives $\kappa_{\mathrm{id},f}=Q_1j$ in the resolution coordinates. Step 6 gives $\epsilon_{X_1,Q_1(f_*I)}=(Q_1j)^{-1}$ in the same coordinates, so their product is the identity. For the right unit law the first morphism is $\mathrm{id}_{X_0}$; use the identity resolution $I\to I$ of its direct image. The comparison $\kappa_{f,\mathrm{id}}$ is then the class of $f_*(1_I)$, while $R_f(\epsilon_{X_0,Q_0I})$ is the identity by Step 6. The product is again the identity. Transport along resolutions exactly as in Step 5 gives both laws at every derived object.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition; explicit coherence calculation using derived.tex Tags 070I (lemma-K-injective) and 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined)

proof.text: An identity-underlying-topos coefficient change is a ringed-topos morphism: its module direct image is restriction of scalars along the structural ring map, as in [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. All resolutions above are taken in the module category for the ring on the relevant $X_i$; the composition normalization applies to these morphisms as well. No step used an isomorphism or flatness of the structural ring map. Consequently the same calculations give every asserted law when any of $f,g,h$ is such a coefficient change.

tool_uses.why: Small ringed-site K-injective resolution existence; a resolution tool, not a replacement of the mate-unit route.
The Hom bijection into K-injectives detects the chain homotopy needed for the common-resolution calculation.
The arbitrary-derived-morphism and change-of-resolution formulas compute the whiskered comparison; the mate unit does not supply these resolution formulas.
The existing normalized ordinary unbounded ringed-topos composition theorem is the input comparison whose coherence is proved here.
Definition of ringed-topos morphism and its additive module direct image, including coefficient restriction.
